status: Five title-control concepts awaiting user selection before adapting the remaining menu controls.

concepts.name: Cutting throat
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: TITLE CONTROL CONCEPT 1 OF 5 — "THE CUTTING THROAT" — a transparent pixel-art game title-banner sprite.
The attached image is the actual original Polar 115 cutter sprite used in this game. DIRECTLY TRANSFORM ITS PHYSICAL MACHINE GEOMETRY into a creative title control, not merely its metallic colors. Ignore the reference's background.
Design one wide, shallow front-view miniature paper guillotine, about 4.5:1 silhouette, centered on a landscape transparent canvas. The title belongs INSIDE THE CUTTER THROAT, printed large on a thick cream-white paper stack clamped under the machine's recognizable brass pressure beam. The paper's exposed top/front makes the title perfectly readable.
Retain the original's recognizable white enamel upper bridge, brass clamp beam with black bolt heads, ribbed black blade throat, thick angled side guard arms, projecting polished stainless front table with small central scalloped notch. The white bridge and guards embrace the title rather than just framing a dark rectangle. Put compact black two-hand pushbuttons in side control pods, and one small red/yellow emergency stop at the right. Strong visual silhouette: this must immediately read as a paper cutter repurposed as a game title sign.
Exact hero title: "THE PICTURE SHOP" on one line, elegant bold readable warm charcoal print on the paper, centered, occupies most of horizontal width. Under it, very small subtitle printed on paper: "PRINT • PACK • KEEP THE DOORS OPEN". Let the ivory paper title face provide open calm space; mechanical details at top, bottom and sides.
Match the reference's polished shaded pixel art, bold dark pixel outlines, restrained industrial greys, ivory enamel, aged brass, black guards and red stop; art has volume, character, plausible machinery and beautifully composed details, not photorealism.
No full standing machine, no floor, no legs or footpedal, no plain rectangular picture frame, no web-card bevel frame, no screws-only border, no neon sci-fi. NO concept number or captions baked into sprite. No background, no checkerboard, no external shadows; genuinely transparent alpha outside silhouette. Produce one finished concept only.

concepts.name: Operator console
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: TITLE CONTROL CONCEPT 2 OF 5 — "OPERATOR CONSOLE" — standalone transparent pixel-art title-banner sprite for The Picture Shop.
Reference image is the game's original POLAR 115 cutter. Creatively reinterpret the actual operator console and white machine head into a wide title control. It must look like a piece of this paper cutter, with its actual physical functions and distinctive silhouette.
ONE wide low horizontal assembly, about4.5:1, from a slightly elevated FRONT view. Make an ASYMMETRIC machine control head: broad ivory enamel bridge stepped in height, an oversized deeply inset charcoal operator LCD on the left/center (about70 percent of width), a compact physical grid of small dark square keypad keys and two rotary knobs in a stout grey pod on the RIGHT. Add the original cutter's unmistakable large red emergency stop on its yellow collar at the rightmost end. A short brass clamp rail with bolt heads and ribbed blade opening sit directly underneath the control head. A narrow stainless feed table projects forward at the base with a couple of flat cream paper sheets and the source's centered table notch. Add black two-hand cut controls at the two lower table corners.
Title is the active screen readout, in large sharp warm ivory/amber luminous typography: EXACTLY "THE PICTURE SHOP" on one line. Small subtitle beneath on the LCD: "PRINT • PACK • KEEP THE DOORS OPEN". Plenty of calm dark display space; no tiny fake software text, no additional labels.
Shaped side cheeks, stepped housings, physical keypad cluster and table create the form; do not wrap a generic rectangular metal frame around a title. Match source shaded pixel art and crisp black outlines, brushed steel, ivory enamel, charcoal guards, brass, small red stop. Restrained, tactile, clear readable title.
No full standing machine, no legs, no floor, no background, no external shadows, no checkerboard. True alpha outside sprite. No concept number/caption. Produce one creative finished sprite.

concepts.name: Feed table
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: TITLE CONTROL CONCEPT 3 OF 5 — "THE FEED TABLE" — transparent pixel-art game title-banner sprite.
Use the input ORIGINAL POLAR 115 cutter sprite as a direct physical design reference, especially the left three-quarter isometric cutter with its broad polished steel tables. This must be a creative transformation of its machinery into a title control.
Design one WIDE low cut-paper title assembly in a gently elevated THREE-QUARTER VIEW, approximately3.8:1 silhouette. Make the stainless feed table a beautiful large foreshortened trapezoid extending toward the viewer, wide across the composition. The title is printed on a thick ivory job-paper stack that slides out across the tabletop, with staggered trimmed paper edges and a few neat small rectangular offcuts on the RIGHT table wing. On the LEFT background corner build the recognizably shaped Polar enamel machine bridge and black ribbed cutting throat; its brass clamp runs diagonally behind the paper. Two substantial sloping guard arms hug the paper's upper corners. A small actual program display/keypad pod is tucked at the rear-left, and red/yellow emergency stop at rear-right. Physical black cut buttons are built into the two front table corners, plus the original table's recessed front-center handhold/notch.
The machine is cropped to HEAD and TABLE only: no large base cabinet or floor, no legs, no footpedal. Make a dynamic asymmetric silhouette and convincing source-like volume rather than a symmetrical rectangular bezel.
Hero typography on the paper, not on a screen: EXACTLY "THE PICTURE SHOP" in large dark charcoal bold serif print, readable and centered across paper despite gentle perspective. Below, small exact subtitle "PRINT • PACK • KEEP THE DOORS OPEN". Paper title area is dominant and calm, use strong high contrast and not too much perspective distortion.
Style: source-matched richly shaded pixel art, crisp black outlines, warm ivory sheets, white enamel body, bright brushed steel table, aged brass clamp rail, charcoal guarded throat, small saturated red stop. Delightful tactile printing-shop character.
No generic metal frame, no floating logo, no additional lettering, no concept number or caption, no background, no checkerboard, no external floor shadows. Truly transparent outside the single cohesive sprite.

concepts.name: Cut-paper letters
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: TITLE CONTROL CONCEPT 4 OF 5 — "CUT-PAPER LETTERS" — imaginative transparent pixel-art game title-banner sprite.
Input reference is the actual original Polar 115 cutter sprite. Use its distinctive guillotine geometry: ivory enamel crosshead, black ribbed throat, brass bolted clamp, sloping guards, stainless table and black dual-hand cut buttons. This concept is about PAPER TYPOGRAPHY integrated with a recognizable cutter, not another framed label.
ONE wide low front-facing miniature cutter head and table, about4:1 silhouette, no cabinets or legs. Its clamp is lifted above the cutting bed, revealing a dark ribbed throat. Filling the open throat and standing on the steel table are huge THREE-DIMENSIONAL LETTERS made from tightly layered ivory paper, thick stacked visible paper edges, hand-crafted from clean geometric paper pieces. The title letters themselves are the hero object, not ink on a rectangular paper label or text on a screen.
Exact wording "THE PICTURE SHOP" in a SINGLE line of bold chunky block-capital paper letters. High readability, warm white front faces, subtle grey layered side edges and dark outline for contrast. Letters occupy70 percent of entire sprite width and40 percent of height, aligned along tabletop. Small paper trimmings sit neatly near the two ends. The outer guard arms support the composition at either side, ivory curved/stepped enamel shoulder housings above; brass clamp bolt row behind/above the letters; small source-like red stop/yellow collar on right shoulder and a tiny dark program control on left. Put the black two-hand pushbuttons in front table corners. Broad steel lip has the actual central notch.
Subtitle is small black print on a narrow paper strip along the table's front ledge: exactly "PRINT • PACK • KEEP THE DOORS OPEN".
Style: beautiful tactile shaded pixel art matching the machine source, readable expressive typography, hard black pixel edges, restrained off-white steel charcoal and aged brass, small warm red accent. Creative and playful industrial title emblem, no modern web-card border.
No boring rectangle frame, no standing full machine, no background, no external shadows, no checkerboard, no labels or concept numbers. Transparent alpha outside cohesive sprite.

concepts.name: Enamel bridge
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: TITLE CONTROL CONCEPT 5 OF 5 — "THE ENAMEL BRIDGE" — transparent pixel-art game title-control sprite.
Use the input original POLAR 115 cutter sprite as the direct structural reference. Transform its white upper machine bridge and twin-handed operator stations into a strong horizontal game emblem. Make it distinctive rather than another paper-on-table design.
ONE wide low FRONT-view assembly, approximately4:1 silhouette: a substantial IVORY ENAMEL MACHINE BRIDGE is the main title-bearing object. Its upper profile has a shaped shallow stepped crown and sloped/beveled shoulders. Title is printed DIRECTLY ON THE WHITE MACHINE HOUSING in big dark charcoal industrial stencil lettering, exactly "THE PICTURE SHOP", single line. No rectangular display surrounds the title and no paper sheet behind its letters. Small exact subtitle "PRINT • PACK • KEEP THE DOORS OPEN" is printed neatly underneath on the same enamel surface.
The bridge descends into two chunky operator-side shoulder pods at LEFT and RIGHT. Each lower pod has a BIG black circular dual-hand pushbutton on its square steel mounting plate, facing viewer, like the original source's cut controls; these are signature sculptural ends of the title control, visibly protruding forward and below the title. Add one smaller RED emergency stop with yellow collar up on the right shoulder. Small compact program display/keypad on upper-left, subordinate to title.
Immediately UNDER the title housing run the actual brass bolted pressure beam and a narrow deep black ribbed cutting throat. Two sloping heavy guard arms angle toward the viewer on either side, and a slim projecting stainless table lip with original central notch grounds the sprite. Tiny freshly cut paper strips on this lip communicate its function, but paper is not the hero.
Distinct shaped silhouette: broad white bridge between sculptural side pods, bevelled shoulders, large tactile cut buttons, recesses and ledge. No legs/base cabinet, no broad flat paper stack, no generic metallic picture frame, no dark title rectangle.
Style: source-matched shaded pixel art, carefully defined black pixel outlines, warm ivory enamel, charcoal stencilled title, brushed stainless, brass bolt row, authentic black guarded throat and tiny red/yellow stop accent. Strong playful mechanical personality, polished and legible as a game banner.
No other text, no concept number, no captions, no background, no checkerboard, no exterior drop shadows. Genuinely transparent alpha outside the silhouette.
